A02-K2-REVERSED is the discriminator: with the low scorer (0.25) evaluated LAST, the next parent is still the high scorer (c01, node 0) -- so score, not recency, decides. Seams: ideation (strategy.py:845), implementation (strategy.py:1036) and the feedback judge (feedback_flow.py:16) are replaced, and the adapter's seams.py enumerates exactly which real runtime functions remain (_select_parent, get_best_experiment, get_deliverable_experiment, checkout_to_best_experiment_branch, enforce_evaluation_integrity, manifest_of_record, select_committed_candidate ...). claims.claim: EvE: the frequency test shows the score drives the selection; pooling, independence, per-iteration counting, competing hypotheses and pre-registered n all hold up.
commands: independent exact two-sided binomial on the pooled replication numbers
claims.observed: HEAD = 979065fd2cf1b3be9caf70596478fe27df7815ad (the pin). base.py:40 sets _rng = rng or random.Random() -> unseeded, fresh entropy per population, so the six replicates in e1_replication.json are independent draws; each replicate builds a fresh population and sampler. My fresh 3000 draws through the real call site: E1 p_hat = 0.7357 (closed form 0.7310586), swap control 0.2553 (closed form 0.2689414), two-proportion z = 37.21, p ~ 5e-303; the results differ from theirs (0.7540 / 0.2630), which is expected with an unseeded RNG and proves the numbers are not hard-coded. Sampler class = RankExponentialSumSampler instantiated by Hydra from the shipped config; my instrumented wrapper counted exactly one sampler.sample call per draw (3000 calls / 3000 iterations) -> the count is per iteration, not per worker, and Phase2BatchRunner._sample_solvers (phase2.py:597-605) samples n_solver_examples_phase2 once per call with the population RNG. Pooled arithmetic reproduced: p_hat 0.7290 and z -0.6228719532600361 exactly, exact two-sided p 0.5339723993557 vs their 0.5339723993507 (agreement to ~5e-12). Competing hypotheses are rejected in the artifact (uniform 0.5 at p=2.1e-119; wrong population 0.731 at p=1.6e-16; re-ranking 0.8808 at p=0.0021). Pre-registered n (43 normal / 44 exact, binding ~515 by their own reading) is met with 2000 iterations, ~4x margin. Honest disclosure present and correct: the single E1 run lands at p=0.020, just under alpha, and is superseded by the pooled figure. Pooling including E1 gives 0.7315 (n=20000), also consistent.

additional_findings.title: The reference fixture's default run dir resolves from the fixture's own location and escapes the adapter root
additional_findings.evidence: conformance/fixtures/adapters/reference_adapter.py:63 sets run_dir = Path(flags.get('run-dir', A0 / 'conformance' / 'out' / 'fixture-runs' / runtime)) with A0 = <fixture dir>.parents[2] (fixture_common.py:17). The runner passes --run-dir only on the `run` fallback path, not on the `conformance` path, so a copy of the fixture placed anywhere else writes its E* state under that copy's grandparent. I hit this: my copy under a0/verify/fixtures/adapters/ resolved A0 back to a0/ and created 143 files in a0/conformance/out/fixture-runs/kindlier (since removed). Harmless for the study as laid out, but any harness that copies the fixture will litter the original tree. Requested fix: take the run dir from an explicit flag/env, or default it under the fixture's own directory. Owner: conformance workstream.
additional_findings.disposition: still open - it bit me twice; my own adapter copies are now patched to write under verify/out/fixture-runs
